desc: The legal representation of the less fortunate is a vital aspect of a just and balanced society. Public and religious courts should therefore handle legal disputes between Commoners and the elites as fairly as possible.
entities.name: Access to Royal & Ecclesiastical Courts

desc: Allows the Commoners to hunt and skin game within the legal and physical boundaries of their lord's or township's domain.
entities.name: Hunting Permits

desc: By sponsoring various trade centers across our realm, we will make sure that Burghers and people of coin have ample facilities in which to exchange wares and establish a healthy flow of trade.
entities.name: Allow Trade Center Sponsorship

desc: Seasoned veterans of Saharan trade, these individuals oversee and drive the caravans of Salt that traverse the inhospitable deserts.
entities.name: Amenokal Salt Traders

desc: Our servitude to the highest authority of the Catholicism faith can never be mere promises. By committing to support the Rome, we are sure to win his favor.
entities.name: Apostolic Tax

desc: Nobility and divinity are concepts that have become increasingly interwoven within our pious society. The crown retains the right to appoint high church officials, which ensures that the beneficiaries remain loyal to the state while gaining influence of their own.
entities.name: Appoint Ecclesiastical Offices

desc: The Sindicat Remença is a peasants' guild or primitive trade union. This was first introduced in Catalonia in 1448.
entities.name: Sindicat Remença

desc: The ''Arte della Lana'' — the Wool Guild — is one of the most powerful of the seven major guilds of Florence, controlling every stage of the wool trade from the purchase of raw fleece to the sale of finished cloth. Its membership encompasses merchants, dyers, weavers, and finishers, all bound by strict quality standards enforced by guild inspectors. Granting formal recognition to the Arte entrenches the influence of the merchant class and ensures that Florence's reputation for fine cloth remains unmatched across the continent.
entities.name: Arte della Lana

desc:
Life in our religious orders has finally returned to its cloistered, austere ideal. The accumulation of wealth is restricted, and monastic focus is entirely set on contemplation and prayer.

Additional monasteries may be created.
entities.name: Austere Monastic Life

desc: Following the advice of our best clerical advisors, we have reformed our monasteries in accordance with Catholicism principles.
entities.name: Monastery Reform of Melk

desc: ''Qāḍī'' should be given greater power within their alloted ''Kadiluk'' jurisdictions, to better utilize their wisdom for the benefit of the state.
entities.name: Autonomous Kadiluks

desc: The local commanders that man the posts of our Order have long demanded increased autonomy, in the name of efficient self-governance and allegiance to our cause.
entities.name: Autonomous Local Commanders

desc: The people of Scotland have been traditionally organized in multiple clans, each one united in both terms of kinship and geographical location, and owing allegiance to their own clan chief. Clan gatherings and interrelation among them is what drives Scottish politics.
entities.name: Autonomous Scottish Clans

desc: For generations, the clans of the rural northern highlands have retained their Gaelic identity, while the clans of the lowlands have largely developed their own Scottish culture. Despite differing practices, the clans of the highlands and lowlands will nevertheless set aside their differences to fight foreign adversaries that threaten Scotland.
entities.name: Autonomous United Scottish Heritage

desc: Nobility receive privileges, but they also have obligations to their Lord. They have to provide troops — ''auxilium'' — and maintain fortifications and infrastructures in the lands they rule, but they also have to give counsel — ''consilium'' — to their Lord when requested.
entities.name: Auxilium et Consilium

desc:
The state is in the hands of the noble and wealthy families who occupy key positions in the Venetian government. To defend the interests of the state and, by extension, of these families, the Council created the ''Avogadoria de Comùn'' - the ''public prosecutors'' - who supervise accounts of high positions, investigate allegations of corruption and prosecute violations of law.
Even the Doges themselves are not spared by their watchful eyes...
entities.name: Avogadoria de Comùn

desc: No one knows the complex power dynamics of far-flung provinces better than the elites who already reside there. Given status as Ayans, they are trusted to govern with only limited oversight from the state.
entities.name: Ayan Notables

desc: The right to establish town councils with clear legislative and executive jurisdictions is a clear and fundamental right of the Commoners within our domain.
entities.name: Ayuntamientos

desc: This type of manorial domination developed under the feudal system and is based on the 'ban', which is the authority of a lord to command his tenants, give them orders, and punish them. This has led to the Nobility having greater power in their domains, since they are the ones who dole out justice within their territories and can also tax the Commoners for most of their economic activities.
entities.name: Banal Lordship

desc: The system of land grants for our elites is inspired by the Byzantine system of ''Pronoias''. It grants them a grand array of privileges and obligations on behalf of their domains when it comes to administering the lands leased to them by the government.
entities.name: Baština Grants

desc: We have divided our dynastic lands justly and in accordance to the law. This will lead to further fragmentation of our lands and a heavily decentralized administration. To emerge as a powerful contender among the princes of the Holy Roman Empire, we will have to assert our control and central authority once more.
entities.name: Bavarian Land Division

desc: The ''Kreditwerk'' controls large parts of our finances, hindering our financial capabilities.
entities.name: Kreditwerk

desc: The ''Kreditwerk'', now reformed under the direct control of the Crown, will enable us to more efficiently finance our projects.
entities.name: Reformed Kreditwerk

desc: Developing our settlements and cities is a costly endeavor. By granting building rights to the local population, we will ultimately reduce the overall end cost of development. However, giving the people such an allowance will considerably increase their influence.
entities.name: Building Rights

desc: Allow rich Burghers to develop our infrastructure by building [
], benefiting both our ever-expanding economy and the traders themselves.
entities.name: Building Roads Rights

desc: The laws regarding land ownership have recently been the matter of much heated debate at court. We shall expand the land ownership rights of our Burghers, with the goal of making the various administrative guilds more compliant in exchange for having been given more power.

mods.label: Maximum RGO Size in Towns & Cities

entities.name: Burghers Land Rights

desc: The wealthy members of our society have gained Religious Protections and are therefore exempt from any conversion attempts from the state.
entities.name: Protected Faith of the Wealthy

desc: The Royal Burgh Commissioners, representing the Crown-chartered burghs of Scotland, convene regularly to safeguard their privileges, regulate commerce, and advise the nation's ruler. Through their collective authority in the Convention of Royal Burghs, they ensure that Scotland's trading communities remain vital to governance, economy, and law, standing as a counterweight to the power of the Nobility and Clergy.
entities.name: Royal Burgh Commissioners

desc: Guilds and other associations of merchants and tradesmen are a necessary evil. By putting a pious cardinal in charge of them, we will ensure that no organization will stray from the path of God, and that the sin of greed will not cloud the minds of our Burghers.
entities.name: Cardinal-Lead Guilds

desc: The borderlands of Castile and León have, over the last few centuries, produced a unique order of knightly shepherds. They are accustomed to spending winters guarding their flocks in border strongholds and spending their summers raiding or waging war against their Islam foes.
entities.name: Caballeros Villanos

desc: We have compiled the scattered laws and customs of our Nobility. This codification of their privileges shall serve as the cornerstone of their elevated status in our realm.
entities.name: Fuero Viejo de Castilla

desc: The Mit'a System is an adaptation of an Incan labor draft that forces indigenous communities to provide rotating labor for our enterprises, especially in silver mines like those of Potosí.
entities.name: Mit'a System

desc: The Regimiento is a system implemented to govern the town and cities of Castile through certain appointed councilmen, who come from the ranks of the richest and most powerful families.
entities.name: Regimiento

desc: The preparation of tributes, sacrifices, and festivals is a great honor for our Burghers. In exchange for this responsibility, they shall be exempt from regular taxation.
entities.name: Ceremonial Tax Exemptions

desc: Deriving from the lesser branches of the Nobility, these administrators are responsible for drafting governmental decisions into legal documents, forming the basis of our administration.
entities.name: Chancellor Nobles

desc: Following the Pugachev uprising, a charter was issued that strengthens the privileges of the Nobility and emphasizes their role in maintaining order.
entities.name: Charter of the Nobility

desc: Our country is home to people of many different beliefs, and coexistence is becoming increasingly difficult, which in turn weakens our government. We must enforce the rule that our subjects may only practice our State Religion in order to quell this disunity — and to consolidate our authority.
entities.name: Enforced Religious Unity

desc: The servants of the faith already possess many skills we look for in administrators. They are well-educated, experienced scribes who follow a higher calling. In many ways, allying ourselves with them would create an efficient and very strong cadre of administrators.
entities.name: Clergy in Administration

desc: We have decided to give the faithful the right to own private land. This will make them more powerful and influential, but will also allow for a more constant presence of holy men at our disposal.

mods.label: Possible Clerics in Towns and Cities

entities.name: Religious Land Rights

desc: Our ancient universities are famous for producing the most influential minds in the land, and so they must be protected and controlled. Graduates are sworn never to lecture outside the walls of these centers of learning.
entities.name: Lecture Oaths

desc: Our religion has many associated works of literature containing the practices, morals, and principles of our faith. Our Clergy should have unlimited access to the written word in order to study the holy texts of our faith.
entities.name: Religious Literacy Rights

desc: The Military Orders were created after the Crusades began, as a means of fusing the discipline and devotion of monks with the martial skill and experience of knights. They spread throughout Christendom, but other religions also developed similar orders when fighting wars of religion.
entities.name: Military Orders

desc: The legates and other emissaries of the Rome are most welcome in our territory. Moreover, we shall also commit to obeying their judgment, and to never interfere in relations between our local Clergy and the Rome.
entities.name: Papal Emissary

desc: The administration of our territory lies in the hands of the state. However, the organization of the Clergy does not follow our provincial systems. Instead, the they organize themselves in Dioceses, which have significant power and influence over the internal affairs of our country.

mods.label: Possible Clerics in Towns and Cities

entities.name: Powerful Dioceses

desc: Holy men and women have gained Religious Protections and are therefore exempt from any conversion attempts from the state.
entities.name: Protected Faith of the Religious

desc: By making matters of religion our foremost priority, we shall forge our nation into a more cohesive whole.
entities.name: Religious Administration

desc: Faith is what keeps our people united, even during the most challenging times. Thanks to the efforts of our Clergy, our people have emerged from their most recent trial unshaken in their beliefs and more faithful than before!
entities.name: Strengthened Faith

desc: We have decided to form a council of advisors, comprised entirely of holy Clergy. This will make them more influential, but also more complacent, as they will be able to express their concerns directly to us and see their interests satisfied.
entities.name: Religious Advisory Council

desc: This system, also known as ''bonnacht'', requires that our lesser chieftains must billet our loyal soldiers in their own holdings at their own expense.
entities.name: Coign and Livery

desc: Trade is the lifeblood of our economy. Thus, we must ensure that our head of state is supported by only the most capable and knowledgeable individuals, adept in matters of maritime and land trade. This will benefit our commercial capabilities at home and abroad.
entities.name: Commercial Advisory Council

desc: A list of grievances put forward following the Pilgrimage of Grace uprising.
entities.name: Commons Petition

desc: Despite the inherently disadvantaged position of the common people, we must nevertheless dictate that all members of the Commoners have the right to establish common flocks of animals and to raise crops in shared fields.
entities.name: Communal Lands

desc: The entrenched middle and upper classes across our domain have long since sunk their claws into our treasury and courts, securing lenient positions and propagating a stagnant ambiance of corruption.
entities.name: Consolidated Corruption of the Wealthy

desc: The unfortunate reality that our religious leaders have a say over our internal politics is only a side effect of the other corrupt deals they have extorted from us under the threat of excommunication.
entities.name: Consolidated Corruption of the Faith

desc: The entrenched members of the upper classes across our domain have long since sunk their claws into our treasury and courts, securing lenient positions and propagating a stagnant ambiance of corruption.
entities.name: Consolidated Corruption of the Elites

desc: The people no longer respect our authority. Indeed, in many cases, they have threatened to take up arms should they be forced to pay their taxes...
entities.name: Consolidated Corruption of the Common People

desc: Protecting the faithful who live far from our capital is an arduous task. By commanding the Nobility in those lands to protect their people, we will shield our people against heathens and heretical foes.
entities.name: Control of the Borderlands

desc: The finances of our nation are a topic of great importance as we strive to improve and perfect our ledgers. Perhaps it would be a good idea to entrust the wealthy members of our society with such a task, and in return provide them with reduced taxation on their commodities and assets.
entities.name: Control over Monetary Policy

desc: Cutting and circulating new coins of adequate quality is a complicated, yet essential process for the development of a sovereign people. By taking control of the coinage, we will strengthen our economic foundations and consolidate our authority.
entities.name: Control over the Coinage

desc: The Cossacks have a distinct and proud identity, with their own traditions and customs. They do not easily abandon them due to outside influences, but stand firm and follow their own way of living.
entities.name: Cossack Identity

desc: Cossacks are traditionally semi-nomadic, not permanently settling in any fixed place for long. Allowing them to retain mobility will go far in preserving their way of life... and in keeping them willing to work for us.
entities.name: Allowed Free Roaming

desc: The freeroaming lifestyle of the Cossacks makes them ideal candidates to send into unclaimed regions and make preparations for establishing permanent settlements.
entities.name: Colonization by the Cossacks

desc: The Cossacks are used to a roaming life, which has taught them to traverse and thrive in almost every type of terrain. We can use these abilities to send them out on expeditions into the unknown, where they will discover new lands for us to take.
entities.name: Exploration by the Cossacks

desc: The harsh life that the Cossacks lead breeds resilient individuals. Instead of permitting them to freely roam our lands, we could recruit the most talented and hardy among them to the administration.
entities.name: Cossack Government Positions

desc: The Cossacks live in their own communities with their own organization. By guaranteeing the autonomy of their territories, we will ensure that they remain loyal to us.
entities.name: Cossack Land Rights

desc: The Cossacks live in a highly militarized society. Instead of allowing them to freely roam the countryside, we shall incorporate them into our military system so that we may take advantage of their battle prowess.
entities.name: Cossack Military Service

desc: The Cossacks are traditionally diverse in their religious beliefs, albeit mostly sharing the same faith. By respecting their personal beliefs, we can avoid breeding religious tensions — not only among themselves, but also between them and us.
entities.name: Protected Faith of the Cossacks

desc: The administration of the Cossacks centers around the ''Rada'', meaning assembly or council, where they decide upon all matters both military and civil. By giving these Rada legal autonomy from our own administration, we can delegate the governance of their territories to themselves, at the same time as we ensure their complacency.
entities.name: Rada Autonomy

desc: Not only shall the Cossacks serve in our military, but shall also be organized with a specific register and their own specific officer ranks, so that they can most efficiently fight in our wars.
entities.name: Registered Cossacks

desc: The Cossacks have their own traditions and social organization. We need to respect these foundational aspects of their culture if we wish them to truly feel like equal members of our society.
entities.name: Respected Cossack Traditions

desc: An ''ataman'' is the leader of a Cossack group. By officially sanctioning their leadership, we will tie them to our rule, albeit at the cost of giving them more authority.
entities.name: Sanctioned Atamans

desc: Many of the lower classes belong to pastoral ''creaghts'', bands of nomadic herders. They migrate seasonally to fresh grazing lands, and are named for the temporary dwellings they build as they move from place to place. As they are not tied to specific land, they exist outside any feudal structure.
entities.name: Creaghts

desc: These courts are dedicated to resolving disputes between our Burghers. They are a powerful branch of our government, and exert enormous influence over commercial and mercantile matters.
entities.name: Dedicated Merchant Courts

desc: Originally a term reserved for Christianity and Israelite communities, the ''Ḏimmī'' refers to the Hinduism and other Dharma believers living in the Islam world. Traditionally, it is the responsibility of the ruler to protect them. However, this is not always as easy, as the ''Ḏimmī'' constitute the majority of the population. But, with the support of the true faith, the ''Ḏimmī'' shall swear loyalty to the state without threatening the tenets of Islam.
entities.name: Dharmic Ḏimmī Communities

desc: The Christianity and Israelite communities are the so-called ''Ḏimmī'' in a Islam state. Traditionally, it is the responsibility of a just ruler to protect these people while keeping them apart from the Islam majority, and the ''Ḏimmī'' community shall swear loyalty to the state without threatening the traditions of Islam.
entities.name: Abrahamic Communities

desc: Our borders are home to many who do not follow our state religion. Their local leaders are keen on maintaining their positions and beliefs. To cooperate with them and share in their wisdom is the natural path to a healthy administration.
entities.name: Grant Administrative Posts

desc: Some of our country's finest administrators follow different faiths than our own, yet are nontheless upstanding and loyal members of our nation. Excluding those who are willing to serve us and the state would be a grave mistake, and we should rectify this immediately.
entities.name: Ḏimmī Bureaucrats

desc: A man's home is his refuge. By guaranteeing property rights to heathen members of our society, we will establish a link of trust between them and our administration.
entities.name: Guarantee Local Land Rights

desc: There are many good citizens in our territory who do not follow our state religion, yet they have been integrated into our legal system and enjoy the same rights as others. Despite protests against their inclusion, allowing them to participate in our judicial framework as witnesses, guardians, and legal representatives of their communities will only further their support of our authority.
entities.name: Legal Autonomy

desc: The secret to a stable multifaith society is simply fair treatment and warm kindness — and, more concretely, tax breaks. By imposing fewer taxes on heathen subjects under our banner, we will ensure their compliance going forward.
entities.name: Lighter Taxation

desc: Parallel to the authority and existence of religio-judicial administration and Sharī'a courts, the Maẓālim operate secularly for the affairs of the unbelievers. Their sessions can take place at the Palace of Justice (''dār al-'adl'') or ceremonial hall within the citadel walls (''īwan kabīr'').
entities.name: Maẓālim Courts

desc: The many heathen believers who peacefully occupy our lands are more than willing to defend their livelihoods and their families, should we permit their recruitment.
entities.name: Allow Military Service

desc: This treaty clearly defines the status, rights, and responsibilities of 'protected persons' within our realm, including Christians, Jews, Zoroastrians, and many other recognized faiths.
entities.name: Pact of Umar

desc: As we strive to maintain social equilibrium, our advisors have deemed it necessary to coordinate with representatives from the many local communities who do not adhere to our state faith.
entities.name: Promote Local Hierarchy

desc: Our people frequently cite a desire to build a more diverse and tolerant society. Acting on their behest and following their example, we will treat non-believers with kindness as we strive to achieve stability and prosperity.
entities.name: Promote Tolerance

desc: Our subjects come from many corners of the earth, and as such, have different believe and lifeways. From lowly fieldhands to displaced members of their former noble classes, they can all boast of the storied histories and beautiful traditions of their people. To respect and allow the practice of diverse customs is the mark of a superior, harmonious society.
entities.name: Preserve Local Traditions

desc: Maintaining the pathways between the many districts of Prague is a contentious topic among the elites. Granting them the right to tax the paving of new roads will inevitably build more connections between our districts.
entities.name: District Taxation

desc: Contrary to the mainstream doctrine, the ancient tradition of our people has been observing both the seventh-day Sabbath on Saturdays and the Lord's Day on Sundays. This privilege codifies those customs into law and protects the peasantry from persecution.
entities.name: Both Days Sabbath

desc: We have decided to imbue the courtly life of our country with the most elaborate formality imaginable. As everyone who is anyone is expected to attend our ruler in the capital, this restricts how much plotting the Nobility can do against us, but it does come at a high cost.
entities.name: Elaborate Court Life

desc: There is no better way to display our magnanimity and strength of faith than to erect major works or architectural splendor, dedicated to the purity of divinity.
entities.name: Embellish Great Works of Faith

desc: To wage war for our faith is the divine calling of all true believers!

mods.label: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

entities.name: Expansionist Zealotry

desc: The armies levied by our people often leave a lot to be desired. In order to protect our people and best our rivals, we must rely on foreign mercenaries, whose contracts will be managed by the elite members of our society.
entities.name: Feudal Mercenary Contracts

desc:
The different artisans and merchants of Florence traditionally are associates in different guilds. This ensures not only a high standard of quality for the products, but also avoids breeding unfair competition. However, the power and influence these guilds hold as a result is undeniable.

This unlocks the [
entities.name: Florence Guilds

desc: Federations and associations of merchants have loosely existed throughout our nation's history. However, we could choose to placate the most powerful traders across our markets by formalizing their participation in a centralized and officially recognized corpus. Such a privilege will undoubtedly impact both our foreign and domestic policies.
entities.name: Formal Guilds

desc: The monarchy is bound by a formalized agreement that requires the rights and freedoms of the estates to be recognized and upheld before an oath of loyalty can be sworn.
entities.name: Formalized Oath of Loyalty

desc: Étienne Marcel's influence has made the Burghers a powerful force in the Estates-General.
entities.name: Leadership of Étienne Marcel

desc: A compromise agreement between the Crown and Étienne Marcel, where the Crown cedes power to Marcel. In return, the Estates-General has granted the request to levy more taxes.
entities.name: Compromise Great Ordinance

desc: Following immense pressure from Étienne Marcel, France is currently governed by terms of Marcel's Great Ordinance. In return for granting him great influence, the state has the backing of the Estates-General to levy more taxes.
entities.name: The Great Ordinance

desc: Through these sanctions, the Catholicism Church in France obtains greater administrative independence from Rome, as it allows electoral appointment to ecclesiastical offices through the means of a general Church council. While these sanctions please the Clergy, our influence and relationship with the Holy See may suffer.
entities.name: Pragmatic Sanction of Bourges

desc: The many teachings of our faith are like the cool shade underneath a great tree, where all may rest and be refreshed. Under this protective canopy of wisdom, our people are encouraged to think deeply about matters of faith, and to expand and diversify our tenets. This freedom of interpretation will allow our religion to adapt to diverse communities while yet maintaining its core principles.
entities.name: Freedom of Interpretation

desc: Since the death of Pap Boniface VIII and the court's relocation to Avignon, most of the cardinals flocking to it are French and under the influence of the France of France, whose grip on the Rome will not allow a return to Rome.
entities.name: French Cardinals

desc: Funding the powerful Burghers known as the Karimi, who are responsible for the trade of spices as well as other valuable goods, is essential to our continued prosperity.
entities.name: Fund the Karimi Merchants

desc: The General Privilege is a list of deals and laws that compels the monarch to guarantee traditional nobiliary rights and to ask for the parliament's permission before declaring war.
entities.name: General Privilege of Aragon

desc: Warriors for the faith, these devoted fighters campaign across distant frontiers in pursuit of plunder, honor, and divine purpose. Comprised of zealous volunteers and tribal raiders, they guard our borders through relentless raids and conquests, spreading both influence and fear in equal measure.
entities.name: Ghazi Lords

desc: A foundational document that enshrines the rights and privileges of the Nobility. By virtue of this treaty, they are granted exemption from direct taxation, ensuring that they suffer no financial burdens from the state's demands. Moreover, this privilege limits their obligations to provide troops, safeguarding their liberties while enhancing their influence in the kingdom.
entities.name: Golden Bull of 1222

desc: The Golden Liberty, also known as ''Złota Wolność'', represents the significant influence and privileges currently held by our Nobility, including the right to elect the ruler and shape national policy. It entailed that all Nobility, regardless of rank, economic status, or ethnic background, were considered equal in power to their peers.
entities.name: Golden Liberty

desc: Our domain is home to many fortifications and formidable strongholds. The maintenance expenses and garrisoning of these emplacements have been entrusted to the local population and townspeople.
entities.name: Gradozidanije and Gradobljudenije

desc: The most important governmental offices within our central administration are reserved for the Nobility within our realm.
entities.name: Great Offices of the Crown of France

desc: The guilds have agreed to divert a portion of their funds toward making improvements to our production process. Though many of these ventures will likely fail, a few may yield breakthroughs that can reshape our capital economy.
entities.name: Guild Investments

desc: The regulated relations between landowners and Commoners will secure some legal protection for our lowest estate, although this will make expanding our farming economy more difficult.
entities.name: Tractatus de Iuribus Incorporalibus

desc: Known for their prolific and influential presence in matters of state, these slaves come from the shores of East Africa. Educated in matters of administration and warfare, they provide a great service in exchange for political influence and, potentially, freedom after religious conversion.
entities.name: Ḥabshī Advisors

desc: Our people have clearly defined roles within their communities. Tasks are distributed and assigned for the collective benefit of the group, with those sharing the same tasks working together. Men and women fulfill complementary roles through their respective assignments, creating a holistic division of labor.
entities.name: Haudenosaunee Labor Division

desc: The post of Iqṭā' holder is not usually heritable. Transforming it into a hereditary one would be unprecedented, and would increase the loyalty of the Nobility.
entities.name: Heritable Iqṭā'

desc: The Hurin Qusqu retain the duty and privilege of serving Inti directly as the ''Villaq Umu'', the High Priest of Inti.
entities.name: Hurin Qusqu High Priesthood

desc: In a bid to forge strong ties with the elite members of our society, we have granted them a series of benefits under the agreement of the Inaugural Diplomas. Among the concessions are reduced levy obligations to the Crown and the right to reduced taxation.
entities.name: Inaugural Diplomas

desc: Encouraging the public to engage with sociopolitical matters is an excellent way to safeguard the health of our nation. If they are more involved with the politics and administration of the country, surely they will work harder to ensure its prosperous future.
entities.name: Increased Civic Engagement

desc: While it is true that most other realms with administrations like ours tend to hold elections for government roles, we have come to realize that if we are to secure the loyalty of the elites, we must allow them exclusive access to hereditary offices.
entities.name: Inherited Offices

desc: By welcoming migrants into our nation, we will build a strong country that benefits from population growth and shifting regional dynamics.
entities.name: Invite German Settlers

desc: A union between the wealthy landowners and the Clergy, wherein legal ownership of the land is transferred to the Clergy to ensure said property can never be confiscated by the nation.

mods.label: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities
Possible Clerics in Towns and Cities

entities.name: Clerical Aristocracy

desc: Patronage of the arts by our Iranian elites has made it possible for extraordinary new styles of art to develop and flourish.
entities.name: Iranian Art Patronage

desc: Since the times of the eastern marches of the Carolingian Empire, German peoples have been expanding and settling further east. Known as ''Ostsiedlung'', this influx of German settlers is often encouraged by local rulers to fill sparsely populated areas. These settlers are subject to a special type of law, the ''Ius Teutonicum'', offering them special privileges like tax exemptions and the right to establish self-governing towns.
entities.name: Ius Teutonicum

desc: Jainism is no longer a dominant or politically favored faith in India, but the Jainism people are far from irrelevant. They have found a niche in moneylending and bureaucracy that makes them an asset to any state willing to offer them patronage.
entities.name: Jainism Banking Rights

desc: While Jainism itself has lost its prominence, it is still a religion with an active minority to consider. Practitioners of this faith are educated and wise scholars who may be a boon our government if we promote them into the administration.
entities.name: Jainism Scholars

desc: Organized by the local administration to perform garrison and auxiliary duties, these fighters were hired to suppress local revolts and ensure the constant flow of reinforcements into our army, while also suppressing rebellions in their home territories.
entities.name: Jaysh Armies

desc: A series of rights granted to the elite members of our country so as to promote integration and uniformity between them and their many peers across the Holy Roman Empire.
entities.name: Joint Assembly Decrees

desc: Justicia de Aragón is a powerful legal and judicial office in the Crown of Aragon, established to uphold regional laws, mediate disputes, and protect the rights of subjects against royal overreach.
entities.name: Justicia de Aragón

desc: By allowing the wealthy members of our society rights over the matters of the Kannada language, we can ensure that our literary oeuvre does not fall into obscurity.
entities.name: Kannada Literature Aid

desc: As a reward for their victories on the battlefield, we grant frontier territories to our military commanders. This helps to solidify their loyalty to us, and improves the influence our capital has over our distant borderlands.
entities.name: Cima Fiefs

desc: The Kaigama is the governor of our Southern territories and the chief of the army. With power, vigor, and tremendous influence, Nobility who hold this title have at times even played the role of king-makers, as they may decide who shall rule.
entities.name: Kaigama

desc: Across the shores of Lake Chad, our Burghers interact and exchange goods with a multitude of folk from faraway lands. This volume of commerce, fully under our control, is the lifeblood of our economy and the foundation of our national stability.
entities.name: Control of Lake Chad

desc: Our empire was built on the backs of our conquered enemies. The flow of forced labor within our nation is a cornerstone of our economy, with frequent raids and conquests further fueling our wealth and power.
entities.name: Serfdom Economy

desc: The Yerima is the governor of our Northern territories and in charge of levying able-bodied fighters to form the lower castes of our armed forces. While not enjoying as much influence as the Kaigama, we may yet come to rely on what sway the Yerima does have when recruiting soldiers, since we continue to struggle against exterior and interior foes alike.
entities.name: Yerima

desc: The Kormlenije System is a mechanism to address the financial and material needs of the Russian Nobility, establishing a financial dependency among the elites. This dependency, in turn, plays a crucial role in securing their unwavering loyalty.
entities.name: Kormlenije

desc: A modified version of the Magdeburg Law, the Kulm Law grants all cities in Prussia that have secured the mercantile interests of the city merchant guilds the privilege of significant autonomy from their overlords.
entities.name: Kulm Law

desc: We pride ourselves on being a nation that takes great care of its Burghers, assuring they have access to legal representation, can move around swiftly as needed, and have the freedom to transport their goods as they see fit.
entities.name: Land of Commerce

desc: Swedish peasants hold a uniquely strong position compared to their peers in much of feudal Europe. They own their land outright, pay taxes directly to the crown, and often have a voice in local assemblies, giving them a degree of autonomy and legal protection. These farmers were not serfs; many are armed and serve in levies. Their rights are rooted in ancient customary law, and their relative independence is a foundational element of Swedish rural society.
entities.name: Land-Owning Peasants

desc: While the ruling Crusader elite may still wield great influence, some of the remaining Greek families still wield considerable power of their own. Finding a compromise between the ruling and formerly powerful elite would be the best way to build a stable rule in Greece.

mods.label: Possible Nobles in Towns and Cities

entities.name: Compromise with the Greek people

desc: While the fall of the Latin empire may have splintered the crusader Nobility, they still maintain a powerful force throughout Greece that cannot be ignored.
entities.name: Crusader Elite

desc: The return of the Crusaders to Constantinople has seen the Patriarchate restored once again. With a strengthened Catholicism presence in Constantinople, the Patriarchate will serve to become the symbol of Catholicism rule in Greece once more.
entities.name: Protector of the Patriarchate of Constantinople

desc: This introduces the requirement for unanimous voting in the Sejm. Any noble could stop any vote or legislation by standing up and shouting ''Sisto activitatem!'' ('I stop the activity!') in Latin, or ''Nie pozwalam!'' ('I do not allow!') in Polish.
entities.name: Liberum Veto

desc: Together with the ''Libro d'Oro'' that list all the noble families of the Most Serene Republic of Venice, the ''Libro d'Argento'' contains the names of all the ''Originarii'' families, who despite being commoners descend from the original inhabitants of the lagoon, and have gained thus the right to trade as citizens of Venice and take jobs in the administration of the Venice.
entities.name: Libro d'Argento

desc: The Great Council of Venice has many rules that determine who is worthy of being a member. One is the ''Libro d'Oro'', which contains a list of families that meet these requisites and can claim to belong to the Nobility of Venice. Only through a great quantity of gold and influence can changes be made to it.
entities.name: Libro d'Oro

desc: The numerous Nobility who follow the Orthodoxy faith deserve equal status to those that do not. By guaranteeing them these rights, they will be more likely to support us going forward.
entities.name: Protection of Orthodoxy Nobility

desc: By integrating the laws of our Ruthenian people, we can more effectively work towards establishing a standard code for the realm.
entities.name: Integrated Ruthenian Laws

desc: Our palatial walls will be adorned with captivating religious scenes created by the nation's most gifted artists, as a way to showcase the beauty of our faith and profess our love towards the divine.
entities.name: Liturgical Mural Art

desc: The many settled tribes across the Maghreb exert great influence over the locals. To appease them and recognize their authority will help us exert control over our domain with greater ease.
entities.name: Tribal Strongholds

desc: A set of privileges that were originally drafted using Flemish law, this legal framework was spread through central Europe via an influx of German immigrants. Aimed at cultivating the liberties of the individual citizen, these rights serve to guarantee and regulate the autonomy of the local administration.
entities.name: Magdeburg Rights

desc: Despite our commitment to republican ideals, we permit the Clergy to retain their traditional privileges and jurisdiction over matters of faith, morality, and church law.
entities.name: Maintain Clerical Proceedings

desc: The ''Muḥtasib'' oversee marketplace integrity by inspecting Burghers, publicly punishing financial criminals, and developing manuals to identify and prevent fraud.
entities.name: Muḥtasib Inspectors

desc: Through centuries of martial tradition, we have refined Furūsiyya, the Islam code of chivalry and military practice, blending horsemanship, archery, and warfare tactics with intellectual and ethical training.
entities.name: Refined Furūsiyya

desc: Our subjects are required to pay tithes to our religious institutions. These mandatory contributions are a divine responsibility, demonstrating the piety and strength of faith our people hold.
entities.name: Mandatory Clerical Donations

desc:
Following a period of political turmoil, the elite members of our society are granted extensive civil liberties to ensure their continued loyalty.

The manifesto remains in effect for the entirety of the current rule, and may prove challenging to revoke.
entities.name: Manifesto of Freedom

desc: The right to hold court, despite not actually being rulers, is quite a valuable privilege for the Nobility. By emulating their liege and claiming the power to arbitrate disputes, levy fines and taxes, and enforce their own laws, they can amass great wealth and command higher authority across their domain — for better or for worse…
entities.name: Manorial Courts

desc: The financing and development of merchant centers will surely attract higher trade traffic, while simultaneously amassing great wealth, ample quantities of various exotic goods, and a reputation for security.
entities.name: Market Fairs

desc: The demands of Masaniello the fisherman are represented in this privilege that protects the common folk from tyrannical taxes, and cushions them in case of economic disaster.
entities.name: Masaniello's Fight

desc: The Jurchen elites are given primacy in state affairs, and are grateful for our refusal to adopt foreign customs.
entities.name: Tribal Favor

desc: Our valuable cloth industry rests upon the shoulders of the finest craftsmen in all of Italy. By entrusting their regulations and production lines to our Burghers, we will attain record profits and productivity at the minor cost of granting our merchant guilds some influence.
entities.name: Milanese Cloth Guilds

desc: With the implementation of the ''mit'a'' system, all males from the ages of fifteen to fifty are required to provide one year of free labor to the government. The labor is regulated so that it does not conflict with each person's ability to provide for their family.
entities.name: Mit'a System

desc: Rather than granting permanent hereditary fiefs to Nobility, the crown retains direct ownership of most lands and appoints temporary administrators to manage them. These officials enjoy the revenues and authority of their territories only while holding office; upon their death or dismissal, control reverts to the crown. This prevents powerful hereditary aristocracies from forming and bolsters administrative loyalty.
entities.name: Monetary Fiefs

desc: A series of laws which grant significant concessions to the Nobility by requiring their approval for new laws, mobilization of armed forces, and new taxes. These statutes also diminished the power of the richest families, and strengthened the position of the broader nobility.
entities.name: Statutes of Nieszawa

desc: The elite members of our society have secured the right to not have any laws made without their consent. Not only that, this privilege also forbids freedom of movement of the serfs and limits rights of the townsfolk.
entities.name: Nihil Novi

desc: It would be wise to follow the teachings of the Christianity Church and decree our serfs and peasants may have respite from their work on Sundays, as a sign of piety and compassion.
entities.name: No Labor on Sunday

desc: At a time where the elites are extremely influential — and can precipitate the rise and fall dynasties — it is fundamentally wise to give them certain key positions in the administrative council.
entities.name: Elite Council

desc: Permitting the Nobility to maintain personal armies is an excellent way to ensure they contribute when we form larger state armies, while also incurring more influence.
entities.name: Noble Armies

desc: One outcome of our feudal system has been the proliferation of castles and forts built by the Nobility as a means of increasing their power and authority. That has had further effects on our society, as the Nobility are able to entrench and fortify themselves within their inherited dominions.
entities.name: Fortification Licenses

desc: Our Nobility believe that they are the only ones capable of leading our armies and navies, due to the events of the past. However, this rankles members of the other Estates, who think that the Nobility are arrogant fools.
entities.name: Only Nobility as Leaders

desc: The Nobility of our country are considered to be peers to our rulers. Therefore, they are eligible to marry into the ruling family, subsequently increasing their influence and power at court, as well as in the government.
entities.name: Royal Marriage Rights

desc: Our mercantile presence must not atrophy. To ensure a robust and continuous stream of trade, it falls upon the shoulders of the Nobility to be the patrons of our Burghers and ensure they have ample coin with which to ferry their goods.
entities.name: Elite Patronage

desc: Several prominent families within the Nobility have taken to sponsoring poets, painters, and scholars in their courts and villas. While some may see this as vanity, such patronage often gives rise to bold new schools of thought and expression, typically in exchange for more influence with the court.
entities.name: Noble Patronage of the Arts

desc: Among the rights Nobility have over the Commoners in their lands, they can tax them, levy them, and exert justice upon them as needed. Peasants living under these conditions become serfs and are usually bound to the land they worked.
entities.name: Nobility Controlled Serfdom

desc: Our navy is maintained and controlled by the Nobility. Thanks to their financial contributions, we will be able to raise a mighty fleet, although in exchange for permitting the Nobility to have more influences over naval affairs.
entities.name: Noble Navy

desc: This represents the privileges our Nobility have over the lands they rule and the people who inhabit them. Among those rights, Nobility can usually tax the Commoners living on their lands, draft them to form levies, or mete out justice on their own. These holdings are usually hereditary.
entities.name: Land Rights

desc: Our Nobility lean towards aggressive military tactics, ascribing to the idea that a good offense is the best defense. Their commanders and soldiers are predisposed toward bold, decisive action, seeking the swift destruction of our enemies.
entities.name: Offensive Military Doctrine

desc: The elites have gained Religious Protections and are therefore exempt from any conversion attempts from the state.
entities.name: Protected Faith of the Elites

desc: The heads of the Ivan's Hundred, our local merchant guild, are permanent members of the commerce court of Novgorod and the ruling council of the Novgorod Republic. With their political presence and the agreements they have made with the Nobility, our nation will surely enjoy continued, successful trade.
entities.name: Ivan's Hundred

desc: Derived from the original set of privileges given to the city of Magdeburg, this legal framework has grown to encompass Western concepts of urban planning, as well as a set of criminal and civil laws, when it spread beyond the core German lands.
entities.name: Novi Fori

desc: Charged with guarding the northern border, the Farima-Soura monitors traffic across the Saharan border, and oversees the safety and swift passage of all mercantile traffic in and out of our borders.
entities.name: Office of the Farima-Soura

desc: The Sankar-Zouma is a prestigious office granted to the Mali by the highest authority in the land. Its role, much like the Farima-Soura, revolves around exercising authority along all trade routes across the southern border.
entities.name: Office of the Sankar-Zouma

desc: To the great dismay of the lowborn, this ordinance has been passed to prevent the spiraling salary costs of the Commoners, effectively fixing wages to pre-plague levels. Employers are also prevented from hiring excess workers, and it is mandatory that all those under the age of sixty must work.
entities.name: Ordinance of Laborers

desc: Originally conceived as a contractual agreement between the Nobility and the government, these statutes spell out the responsibilities of central authority and outline various undertakings in areas like foreign policy, taxes, military matters, and more.
entities.name: Pacta Conventa

desc: The lands of the wealthy are often tilled by Commoners, slaves, or serfs. Thus, the least we can do is award the common people with access to a portion of that land's yield every year.
entities.name: Partial Yield

desc: The upper classes are vultures, devouring the fruits of hard peasant labor and contributing nothing in return. By seizing the means of production, we will place the future of our nation and its people in our own hands!
entities.name: Means of Production

desc: The common people are allowed to keep their weapons, which they then must use when called for levy service.
entities.name: Common Militias

desc: In the rural settlements of our state, there is a saying: 'The laws of the sovereign end at the village's gate.' The people in our settlements organize themselves independently from the central authority of this country.
entities.name: Autonomous Villages

desc:
The Commoners are the lifeblood of our state. They nourish our population, craft the materials for our buildings, and produce the goods our Burghers trade in.
Although war is a time of great hardship for our state, we must make the effort to keep our Commoners away from the conflict if we want to avoid famine and economic collapse after the war.
entities.name: Fewer Levies

desc:
People are the most valuable asset of any state. Famines and discord would be the norm without them. Yet, the elites see them only as property — as possessions to hoard upon their ill-gotten lands!
By granting free mobility to the masses, their fate will be own hands once again, allowing them to leave the lands of their former masters and move to new, more fruitful fields.
entities.name: Free Mobility for the Common People

desc: By involving the most skilled amongst the Commoners in our government, we can improve and expand the reach of our administration into the most remote areas of our territory.
entities.name: Commoners in the Administration

desc: Following Wat Tyler's uprising, the punitive poll tax is abolished and insurances are given that it will not be reintroduced.
entities.name: Exempt from Poll Tax

desc: The common people have gained Religious Protections and are therefore exempt from any conversion attempts from the state.
entities.name: Protected Faith of the Common People

desc: Granting our lower populace a seat in our main assembly will give a voice to the Commoners, of our country and ensure greater rights for them.
entities.name: Represented in Parliament

desc: Freeholdeers with small land possessions receive elevated rights in return for taking on some responsibilities of petty nobles, including having to fulfill higher expectations regarding the defense of the realm.
entities.name: Yeomanry

desc: Expansions have been made to Versailles allowing for members of the France to take up permanent residence at the palace alongside the France family. While those not of the France family enjoy the luxuries of the palace, it has come at the cost of greatly diminished political influence, in order to maintain the favor of the France. This abandonment of their personal estates has also left less room for political intrigue and plotting, making them beholden to the rule of Versailles.
entities.name: Permanent Residence in Versailles

desc: The main bureaucratic corps of our country is made up of highly educated specialists and administrators who manage the daily tasks and support the structure of the government.
entities.name: Petty Bureaucracy

desc: The Treaty of Hadiach concedes many powers and rights to the Cossacks, the most important concession of which being the inclusion of their nation in the Commonwealth, forming the Polish-Lithuanian-Ruthenian state.
entities.name: Treaty of Hadiach

desc: This privilege grants the Orthodoxy Nobility many of the privileges and assurances that have been granted exclusively to the rest of our elites.
entities.name: Empower Orthodoxy Nobility

desc: A seal bearing the insignia of our central authority, this document permits free, uninterrupted travel for our Burghers, allowing them more expedient passage between cities for themselves and their goods in exchange for a small supplemental tax.
entities.name: Polish Merchant Seal

desc: The anarchy and disobedience in the city of Rome and the other Italian estates greatly increased after the Rome moved the court to Avignon. Now those territories are under the control of powerful Italian families such as the Colonna and Orsini, who are almost completely independent of the Rome.
entities.name: Powerful Italian Families

desc: The Nobility of our country has proven to be key allies, as they support most of our enterprises and are the backbone of our armies. For this reason, they consider themselves our equals, and they have become so crucial to the government that we must consult with them before making important decisions.
entities.name: Primacy of Nobility

desc: In order to expand our naval capabilities without having to maintain a large standing fleet, we shall regulate and officially oversee acts of piracy that benefit the nation. Our privateers operate under official sanction, sharing their plunder with the crown in exchange for legal protection. However, the fine line between privateering and piracy requires us to be cautious if we do not wish to damage our international reputation…
entities.name: Privateer Contracts

desc: The elite members of our society have been bestowed with a wide range of rights, in exchange for allowing a foreign heir rule the state. Furthermore, they will no longer be burdened with taxes without their consent.
entities.name: Privilege of Koszyce

desc: The basis of a strong and coherent society is essentially the promotion of one culture to unite all our people and protect them from foreign influences.
entities.name: Promote Cultural Unity

desc: To further elevate [game concept ROOT] as the center of Islam learning, we must ensure more scholars enter our administration, despite the allegiances they might have.

mods.label: Invite Religious Figure from New School Cost
Invite Religious Figure from Same School Cost

entities.name: Promotion of Islam Scholars

desc:
The Rajputs are an ancient caste of honorable warriors and proud nobles. While the rugged land of Rajputana is the heart of their power, Rajput Nobility can be found throughout northern India, and many great Rajas claim Rajput descent.

''Modifier scales with the percentage amount of Mewari, Harauti, Dhundhari, Shekhawati, and Mewati present in our country + extra 100%.''
entities.name: Rajput Society

desc: Many of our settlements, both urban and rural, have become increasingly autonomous under their landholding elite. While recognizing these breakaways as legitimate entities may reduce our control over their affairs, it will nevertheless please the Nobility.
entities.name: Recognized Communes

desc: In exchange for their loyalty to our central authority, we can reduce or do away with military obligations for those who embrace a life of faith in the arms of the divine.
entities.name: Reduced Military Obligations

desc: In an effort to secure the favor and allegiance of our society's upper echelons, we have decided to grant them this this privilege, alleviating them of many of their responsibilities.
entities.name: Reduced Responsibilities for the Elites

desc: The upper echelons of our society hold significant influence and power and, as such, their whims and opinions carry great weight. If we do not want them to tip the balance of power towards their estate, we must allow them certain tax concessions.
entities.name: Reduced Taxation for the Elites

desc: Good diplomacy is difficult to maintain; it only takes a few simple misunderstandings for the relationship between two countries to sour completely. By sending particularly pious diplomats to our brethren in faith, we shall rely on the strength of that commonality to build fruitful, lasting political relationships.
entities.name: Religious Diplomats

desc: The France family has extended an offer of residence for members of the prominent Nobility dynasties to live in the palace of Versailles.
entities.name: Residence in Versailles

desc: The German Nobility maintains the long-standing tradition of dividing the lands and titles of the father between all of the sons, ensuring the peace between brothers and avoiding unnecessary wars.
entities.name: Right to Inherit

desc: Royal Factories are state-sponsored, but privately owned enterprises granted royal privilege and oversight. They operate under official sanction to bolster domestic industry while retaining commercial autonomy.
entities.name: Royal Factories

desc: The scarcity and high price of Salt has resulted in economic hardships for the Commoners. They are hereby exempt from any tax on Salt in order to quickly alleviate economic hardships and reduce social unrest.
entities.name: Salt Tax Exemption

desc:
Our elite class is composed of wise government officials and politicians who gained their enviable positions by proving their knowledge in the national examinations.
The families of these officials may maintain their privileged status as long as they produce at least one official every three generations.
entities.name: Scholar Officials

desc: Through these Statutes, the clans of the rural highlands are expected to send their heirs to be educated in the schools of the lowlands. While this will bring about a more educated generation of highland Nobility, it risks eroding centuries of cultural heritage.
entities.name: Statutes of Iona

desc: The people of Scotland have been traditionally organized in multiple clans, each one united in both terms of kinship and geographical location, and owing allegiance to their own clan chief. Clan gatherings and interrelation among them is what drives Scottish politics.
entities.name: Scottish Clans

desc: Victory always tastes sweeter when our great clan hoards the spoils. However, by sharing them, we will breed goodwill with other powerful clans, which can be used to our advantage later.
entities.name: Share of the Spoils

desc: Granting favorable state-sponsored contracts to wealthy members of our society will allow us to adopt a more efficient grasp on our shipwright processes and cut down on the regulatory red tape around the industry.
entities.name: Shipwright Contracts

desc: Organized militia of Burghers and craftsmen aimed at practicing drills and defending their city against all outside invaders. These associations are permitted by the Crown to don special uniforms and display emblems that are otherwise only permitted to the Nobility.
entities.name: Shooting Societies

desc: The Signoria of Florence is the name of the council of nine that governs the city, its members taken from the different guilds. Every two months, a lottery is held to reelect the council members. This constant shuffling ensures that the interests of the Republic prevail over personal ones. The fact all its members come from the guilds, though, makes it so that the same families are always the ones in charge.
entities.name: Signoria Council

desc: Maritime trade is a valuable source of revenue for our treasury. By granting exclusive contracts to our Burghers, we can regulate commerce while ensuring consistent tax income from shipping and trade.
entities.name: Sponsored Maritime Contracts

desc: Circulating printed religious texts is an excellent way to spread literacy and entrench the teachings of our faith firmly within our people's hearts. These efforts to distribute religious literature will educate our people and remind them of their religious responsibilities.
entities.name: Sponsor Printing of Religious Texts

desc: All government officials in our domain must swear allegiance to the one true faith under the blessing of the Clergy before they may take office.
entities.name: State Official Oaths

desc: These statutes are a symbol of the Nobility's efforts to consolidate their privileges, and the grip that serfdom and aristocracy have on power. Through the weakening of the lower social classes and towns, the Nobility seek to assert their influence.
entities.name: Statutes of Piotrkow

desc: Our faith is served by devout men and woman who dedicate their lives to the care and the spiritual well-being of our people. It is only natural that they are not forced to pay any tithe to the government.
entities.name: Tax Exemption

desc: The Ryad is the given name to the contract signed between the Boyars and the state. It protects the interests and powers of the Boyars while also defining the responsibilities and rights of the Prince.
entities.name: The Ryad

desc: The exemption of merchant vessels from paying dues to transport their goods will certainly go a long way towards ensuring that the Burghers approve of our administration.
entities.name: Toll & Tariff Exemptions

desc: Giving the most powerful merchants in our countries exclusive trading rights to our mercantile goods to powerful merchants will greatly increase the influence of our most prominent traders. This policy will influence our national attitude towards foreign merchants.
entities.name: Trade Monopolies

desc: By granting the oversight of our treasury to wealthy, powerful members of our society, we will secure their interests and increase their loyalty to us, albeit at the expense of losing some tax revenue.
entities.name: Treasury Rights

desc: Our forefathers, and their fathers before them, venerated living life freely outside the walls of settlements. We would do well to follow their example, distancing ourselves from the outside influences seeking to seduce our people away from their true path...
entities.name: Tribal Autonomy

desc: Breeding the strongest horses shall be the cornerstone of our powerful host. By entrusting the process to our Nobility, we will ensure that we will never run out of mounts for our legendary warriors.
entities.name: Tribal Host

desc: Regular gatherings of our tribal communities are an excellent forum in which to discuss politics, exchange information, and negotiate the flow of business to many settlements across our realm. Therefore, we shall allow them.
entities.name: Allow Gatherings

desc: The cultivation and husbandry of Livestock we have procured through warfare and raiding is an excellent way to safeguard the prosperity of our tribal people.
entities.name: Creach

desc: By fostering the next generation of tribal members in neighboring families, their unique knowledge will be passed down, and bonds of kinship and alliance between communities will be strengthened.
entities.name: Fosterage

desc: Our tribal communities are an important cornerstone of our state. It is only right that we allow those willing to contribute to our administration to serve in high positions.
entities.name: Tribal Cabinet

desc: Expanding and respecting the land rights of the many tribal communities in our realm is an excellent way to ensure their continued cooperation.
entities.name: Tribal Land Rights

desc: By engaging in contractual conscription work, many members of our tribal communities enter into the service of our most influential families.
entities.name: Manrent

desc: By granting pasture access to our tribal communities, we can utilize their advanced knowledge about growing crops and raising Livestock.
entities.name: Pasture Access

desc: Those who dwell in the wildest stretches of our land sometimes subscribe to different beliefs. As they are loyal subjects under our banner, we would do well to respect their religious differences.
entities.name: Protected Tribal Faith

desc: The fascinating traditions followed by members of the tribal communities in our society should be respected, and supported by the state.
entities.name: Respected Tribal Traditions

desc: For generations, the clans of the rural northern highlands have retained their Gaelic identity, while the clans of the lowlands have largely developed their own Scottish culture. Despite differing practices, the clans of the highlands and lowlands will nevertheless set aside their differences to fight foreign adversaries that threaten Scotland.
entities.name: United Scottish Heritage

desc: Our tribal warriors are famed for their warfare experience. To employ these hard men within our armies will only serve to empower our forces and further secure our domain.
entities.name: Allow Tribal Levies

desc: Despite our local tribal communities living a life largely detached from that of our mainstream society, we should nevertheless ensure that they are properly accounted for in our registry.
entities.name: Expanded Registry

desc: Anatolia is connected to Tabrīz and Persia through a reliable network of trunk roads. As we directly control one of its critical junctions, our Burghers reap great benefits.
entities.name: Trunk Road to Erzurum

desc: Our realm is home to a diverse population, which occasionally leads to conflict. If we permit our people to remain armed, these minor squabbles could explode into all-out war. It is for that reason our Commoners may no longer carry any weapons on their persons.
entities.name: Banned Weapons for Commoners

desc: The Tysiatskii are military leaders selected from the Boyars. While in other states their responsibilities lie mostly in commanding our soldiers, our Tysiatskii Office serves additional functions as the representative of the Commoners, as acting judges in the commercial court, and as supervisors of our fortifications.
entities.name: Tysiatskii Office

desc: Instead of allowing the lower strata from being exploited by the rich, we shall grant and guarantee basic human rights to the Commoners.
entities.name: Kholop Protection Rights

desc: Despite resistance from the Crown, the '''Union of Aragon''' has forced this set of agreements into law. It provides extensive rights to the Aragonese Nobility and the city-dwelling people at the expense of the ruler's traditional powers.
entities.name: Privilege of the Union

desc: A movement of radical Hussitism focused around the bare elegance of preaching and worshipping, focusing on excluding powerful individuals from the Burghers and Nobility while promoting the mother tongue and simplified ceremonies during communion.
entities.name: Unity of Brethren

desc: It has become clear to us that the future will dawn within city walls. To promote and usher in this new era of urbanization, city-dwellers will be given several grants to promote urbanization across our realm.
entities.name: Urban Development Grants

desc: Our agreement with the Catholic Church will stabilize our relations. However, we will have to cede some power to the Clergy in order to appease the Roman forces.
entities.name: Concordat of Wien

desc: Instead of focusing only on the Hinduism aspect of our nation, we should allow our other religious minorities the right to publically practice their faith.
entities.name: Allow Religious Practices

desc: The Hinduism deities are numerous, and it is better for our people if we grant them rights to worship whichever gods they prefer.
entities.name: Patronization Rights of Minor Deities

desc: The Tamil Nadu is home to many great mercantile cities of the Tamil people. By granting them trade and autonomy privileges, we can ensure their loyalty and value to the state.
entities.name: Tamil Trading Rights

desc: Several of our market towns have experienced considerable growth in recent decades. As a result, they have become symbols of the expansion of the Crown's power throughout the kingdom, in opposition to the feudal lords who dominate the countryside.
entities.name: Villes Franches

desc: The Duchy of Milan under the Visconti family is marked by a fractured and decentralized state. Different prominent members of the Visconti house, including Azzone, Gian Galeazzo, and Bernabò, vie for supremacy through various tactics such as alliances, betrayals, and military campaigns. This constant power struggle constantly weakens the central authority of the Duchy of Milan and contribute to a state of instability and fragmentation in the region.
entities.name: Visconti City States

desc: Our borderlands must be safely guarded at all times. To that end, the system of ''krajine'' splits our frontiers into well-administered districts under the command of local lords, known as ''Krajiška Vlastela'', who are in charge of maintaining and protecting the people of their provinces.
entities.name: Krajiška Vlastela

desc: To demonstrate our piety and religious dedication, we will grant ''waqf'' payments as charitable endowments, which shall be used to fund madrasas, hospitals, and mosques, as well as to aid the less fortunate.
entities.name: Waqf Payments

desc: A jurisprudent framework across our lands that is imbued with legal authority to pass judgment on a variety of crimes.
entities.name: Warrior Tribunal

desc: The Zamindar are feudal rulers who govern our territories autonomously or semi-autonomously. While they are owners of the land they administrate and part of our nobility, in the end, they serve as internal vassals to the Crown itself. In times of war, it is the right of the Zamindar to collect taxes to support our war efforts. Granting this privilege will greatly increase our income — but also the power of the Nobility...
entities.name: Zamindar Tax Privilege

desc: The governing councils of the Venice of Venice choose their members from among the Nobility. These elites come together in so-called ''Zontas'' and have privileges and duties to safeguard the constitution against the accumulation of power by a single ruler.
entities.name: Zonta

desc: The compartmentalization and division of our society is detailed in the various legal frameworks that surround our administrative branch. The most important aspect of our society and bureaucracy is the division of our provinces into Župa districts, aimed at improving how local affairs are handled.
entities.name: Župa Districts
